The national launch built on an earlier history of school meals in India. Food-grain support, cooked meals and later expansion were separate stages. Nutrition, attendance and classroom learning are related aims, but a programme’s launch date does not establish results for each.
Disability rights receive a wider statutory framework

The Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 was enacted on 1 January 1996. It addressed education, employment, a barrier-free environment and social security.

The Act’s title carries 1995, while its enactment date falls in 1996. Its scope placed participation and access within the legal framework. Evaluating implementation requires attention to accessible institutions and enforcement, beyond the presence of statutory provisions.

After the 1996 election, Vajpayee’s BJP government failed to secure a parliamentary majority. United Front governments led by H. D. Deve Gowda and then I. K. Gujral followed, with outside Congress support.

BJP-led governments followed the 1998 and 1999 elections. The alliance government formed after the 1999 election lasted until 2004. Coalition politics involved both short-lived arrangements and governments able to remain in office for several years.
PESA adapts local government to Scheduled Areas

The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act was enacted on 24 December 1996. It extended Part IX of the Constitution to Scheduled Areas with modifications, including a Gram Sabha role in safeguarding traditions, cultural identity and community resources.

PESA addressed a specific constitutional category of territory, rather than every village with a tribal population. Its relationship with state legislation and administrative practice is central to understanding how local self-government worked beyond the 1992 amendments.
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India was established with effect from 20 February 1997. Its role included regulating telecom services and tariffs as private operators entered the sector.
A separate tribunal, TDSAT, took over adjudicatory and dispute functions following the 2000 amendment. Market entry, regulation and dispute resolution became distinct parts of the telecom framework.
The Supreme Court sets workplace sexual-harassment safeguards

In Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, decided on 13 August 1997, the Supreme Court laid down guidelines to prevent sexual harassment at workplaces and provide complaints procedures. The Court directed observance of the safeguards pending legislation.

The guidelines formed an important stage before the dedicated workplace-harassment statute of 2013. Judicial directions, employer procedures and effective remedies were separate steps. The judgment placed workplace safety within the constitutional guarantees of equality and dignity.
India conducted nuclear tests on 11 and 13 May under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Pakistan conducted its own tests later that month.
India openly asserted nuclear weapons capability. This did not make India a recognised nuclear-weapon State under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, which uses a different legal definition.
A national highway network takes shape
The National Highways Development Project and Golden Quadrilateral became major infrastructure priorities under the Vajpayee government.
The four-city highway network was built in stages across subsequent years. Announcement, construction and completion were separate milestones.
The Lahore Declaration seeks dialogue and nuclear risk reduction

Vajpayee and Pakistan’s prime minister Nawaz Sharif signed the Lahore Declaration on 21 February 1999. The initiative sought stronger dialogue and steps to reduce the risk of accidental or unauthorised use of nuclear weapons.
The declaration followed the previous year’s nuclear tests and preceded the Kargil conflict. The diplomatic commitment and subsequent military events form separate parts of the relationship.
Indian forces fought to recover positions occupied by infiltrating Pakistani forces on the Indian side of the Line of Control in the Kargil sector.
The conflict followed the 1998 nuclear tests and the 1999 Lahore diplomatic initiative. Nuclear capability did not prevent limited conventional conflict.
Software exports and IT-enabled services expanded as Indian firms served overseas clients. Skills, telecom links and policy changes helped the sector grow.
The industry offered a new route into global markets. Its growth was concentrated in particular cities and occupations, rather than representing every part of the economy.
Electronic records gain a statutory framework

The Information Technology Act was enacted on 9 June 2000 and came into force on 17 October. It provided legal recognition for electronic records and digital signatures, alongside provisions addressing computer-related offences.

This helped establish a framework for electronic transactions and government filing. Later amendments changed the law substantially. Provisions added afterwards should not be presented as part of the original 2000 text.
Three new states redraw the Union

Chhattisgarh was formed on 1 November, Uttaranchal on 9 November and Jharkhand on 15 November 2000. They were carved out of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar respectively. Uttaranchal was later renamed Uttarakhand.

State reorganisation continued long after the linguistic changes of 1956. These movements also raised questions of regional identity, representation and development. Creating a state and improving public outcomes within it are separate historical questions.
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan expands the elementary-school effort
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan was launched in November 2000 and developed as a national programme for universal elementary education. It supported school access, facilities and teaching provision.

Its implementation extended across later governments. Enrolment, attendance, completion and learning are different outcomes. The programme preceded the 2002 constitutional amendment and the later commencement of the right-to-education framework.
Rural roads become a national programme
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana launched on 25 December 2000 to improve rural road connectivity, including all-weather access for eligible unconnected habitations.

This was a different infrastructure task from widening highways between major cities. A completed road, its maintenance and its effect on access to schools, health care and markets each require separate assessment.
A major earthquake devastates Kutch and other parts of Gujarat

A powerful earthquake struck the Kutch region of Gujarat on 26 January 2001. Bhuj and other towns and settlements suffered extensive destruction, prompting rescue, relief and a long reconstruction effort.

The disaster exposed the importance of building safety, local capacity and recovery planning. Immediate rescue and rebuilding livelihoods were different tasks. Its place in disaster-management history precedes the 2004 tsunami and the national legislation of 2005.
A terrorist attack reaches the Parliament complex
Terrorists attacked the Parliament complex in New Delhi on 13 December 2001. Security personnel and others died defending the institution.

The attack became a major national-security crisis. Its immediate history and the later investigations, prosecutions and judgments need to be read separately. Parliamentary commemorations preserve the record of those killed.
Gujarat violence and the demand for justice

The burning of a train at Godhra on 27 February 2002 was followed by large-scale communal violence in Gujarat. The National Human Rights Commission examined protection, relief, investigation and accountability.

The NHRC later sought Supreme Court intervention in the Best Bakery case, including an independent investigation and a retrial outside Gujarat. Its concerns illustrate why witness protection and credible trials form part of the history, alongside the violence itself.
Parliament enacts the constitutional right-to-education provision
The 86th Constitutional Amendment received assent on 12 December 2002. It provided for Article 21A, covering free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen.

It also revised Article 45 on early childhood care and added a parental duty. The amendment and the later RTE legislation became operational in April 2010. Enactment in 2002 and commencement in 2010 are separate milestones.
Delhi Metro begins with the Shahdara–Tis Hazari corridor
Delhi Metro’s first corridor, between Shahdara and Tis Hazari, was commissioned on 24 December 2002. DMRC records the opening for passenger service on 25 December.

The initial corridor was one stage of a much larger network developed later. Its opening adds urban public transport to the highway and rural-road story. Network expansion, ridership, affordability and connections with other transport require separate assessment.
Electricity reform consolidates the sector’s legal framework

The Electricity Act was enacted on 26 May 2003, with most provisions taking effect on 10 June. It consolidated the framework for generation, transmission, distribution, trading and use of electricity, and addressed competition, consumer interests, tariffs and regulatory institutions.

A national legal framework did not immediately create reliable or affordable supply in every area. Investment, distribution finances, regulation and delivery remained practical tests of reform. Electricity adds an essential public-service dimension to the era’s account of infrastructure.
Fiscal management gains a statutory framework

The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted on 26 August 2003. It established a framework for fiscal responsibility, transparency and medium-term management of Union government finances.

The Act came into force on 5 July 2004. Its original framework, subsequent amendments and actual fiscal outcomes are different parts of the story. A deficit target is not evidence of a target being achieved.
New central-government entrants move to contributory pensions

A notification of 22 December 2003 introduced the defined-contribution New Pension System from 1 January 2004 for new entrants to Central Government service, except the Armed Forces. The scheme later became known as the National Pension System.

The initial change concerned a defined group of new employees. It was distinct from later access for other subscribers and from PFRDA’s later statutory status. Contributions and investment performance became central to the pension design.

The Reserve Bank of India’s Real Time Gross Settlement system went live on 26 March 2004. It enabled funds transfers to settle individually in real time, rather than through netting of multiple transactions.

RTGS was a change in banking and payment infrastructure distinct from the later retail-payment systems. The launch date preceded wider participation and later changes to operating hours and access. It shows how financial modernisation also depended on settlement systems behind customer transactions.
overview: Start with the 1991 crisis and the institutions that followed. Rupee adjustment preceded the July Budget and industrial-policy changes. Exchange-rate reform continued through 1992–1994. The securities scandal exposed weaknesses in oversight; electronic equity trading and, later, RTGS changed market and payment infrastructure. PSLV’s successful 1994 flight adds another path of technological development.

Follow public protection alongside changes of government. Coalition bargaining gave regional parties a larger national role. Local-government amendments, PESA and the Bommai judgment addressed different parts of federalism. Human-rights oversight, disability law and the Vishaka guidelines widened routes to protection and participation. National AIDS control and Pulse Polio addressed different public-health challenges.

Internet access, telecom regulation and software exports changed several industries. School nutrition, education, rural roads, Delhi Metro and electricity reform addressed other needs. The Gujarat earthquake exposed the demands of rescue and reconstruction. These developments shared a period with Lahore diplomacy, Kargil and the Parliament attack. Contributory pensions and RTGS began before the 2004 change of government; the next chapter follows the expansion of rights-based welfare.

eras.title: Economic Expansion & Rights-Based Governance
eras.question: How does growth become an entitlement?
eras.intro: The UPA governments led by Manmohan Singh combined economic expansion with new rights to information, work, education and food. Public-health programmes and space missions reached major milestones. The global financial crisis, terrorist attacks and disputes over corruption tested the government’s capacity and public trust.
eras.tension: A legal entitlement gave people a stronger basis to make a claim. Access still depended on schools, clinics, local administration, timely payments and credible remedies. Growth and new programmes expanded possibilities while inflation, financial volatility and unequal access remained pressing concerns.
events: A Congress-led alliance forms the government
Manmohan Singh became prime minister on 22 May 2004, leading the United Progressive Alliance after the general election.

The change of government continued the era of coalition politics. The UPA combined economic reform with a larger programme of welfare legislation and public-service spending, with delivery becoming a central political test.
The Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami of 26 December 2004 devastated coastal communities, including in India. It exposed gaps in the region’s warning and preparedness systems.

India subsequently established its tsunami early-warning centre at INCOIS, operational from October 2007. Detecting a hazard, communicating warnings and enabling communities to act are separate parts of preparedness. A warning system does not eliminate the underlying risk.
A mission to strengthen rural public health

The National Rural Health Mission launched on 12 April 2005 to improve accessible, affordable health care in rural areas. In 2013 it became one of the two sub-missions within the National Health Mission, alongside the urban mission.

Strengthening local health services is a different policy task from financing hospital treatment. Both matter to access. Announced coverage and institutional design do not, by themselves, establish service quality in every district.
The right to ask the state for information

The Right to Information Act was enacted on 15 June 2005 and came fully into force on 12 October. It created a national framework for citizens to seek information held by public authorities, subject to specified exemptions.
It gave citizens a route to seek records and challenge refusals. Transparency depended on functioning information commissions, record keeping and enforcement.
Rural employment becomes a legal guarantee

The employment guarantee law was enacted in 2005 and launched in 200 districts on 2 February 2006. It guarantees at least 100 days of unskilled manual work per financial year to a rural household whose adult members volunteer for it.

The entitlement is per household, not per individual. Rollout expanded in stages, and NREGA was renamed MGNREGA in 2009. The legal guarantee, work demanded, employment provided and wages paid are distinct measures of implementation.

The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act came into force on 9 September 2005. Under the amended Section 6, daughters of coparceners became coparceners by birth with the same rights and liabilities as sons in the relevant Mitakshara joint-family property.

The reform should not be described as the first time daughters could inherit under the 1956 Act. Its specific significance lay in changing coparcenary rights. Individual disputes also depended on the legislation’s terms and later judicial interpretation.
Domestic violence gains a wider framework for protection

The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was enacted on 13 September 2005 and came into force on 26 October 2006. It provided for protection orders, residence-related relief and other remedies.

The law recognised forms of abuse beyond physical assault, including economic abuse. Its remedies required access to protection officers, courts and support services. Enactment did not remove the barriers faced by survivors.
A national mission links urban investment with governance reform

Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission launched on 3 December 2005. It supported urban infrastructure and services, including basic services for the urban poor, while seeking reforms in city governance and service delivery.

The mission brought municipal institutions into the national development story. Water, sanitation, transport and housing required coordination across city and state agencies. Sanctioning a project was only the start; construction, maintenance and access determined the service residents received.
Disaster management gains a national legal framework
The Disaster Management Act was enacted on 23 December 2005. Its original framework provided for national, state and district authorities, planning and coordination for disaster management.

The Act’s enactment and the later operational development of institutions were different steps. This entry describes the 2005 framework, not every later amendment. Disaster governance also includes prevention, preparedness and recovery, beyond emergency relief alone.
Forest dwellers’ rights receive statutory recognition

The Forest Rights Act received assent on 29 December 2006 and came into force on 31 December 2007. It provided for recognition of rights of forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers whose rights had not been adequately recorded.

The framework included individual and community rights and processes for recognising them. Conservation policy and the rights of forest communities therefore need to be read together. Enacting the law and recognising a particular claim were different steps.
Reservation expands in covered central educational institutions

The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 was enacted on 3 January 2007. It provided for 27 per cent OBC reservation alongside SC and ST reservations in the institutions it covered.

The law contained exclusions, including for minority educational institutions. Its scope concerned admissions, distinct from the Union employment policy upheld in the Mandal judgment. Implementation and judicial scrutiny formed further stages of the policy.
Health insurance targets poor households in the unorganised sector

Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana launched on 1 October 2007 and became operational on 1 April 2008. Its initial design provided smart-card-based cashless health insurance of ₹30,000 per family per year for eligible below-poverty-line families of up to five members in the unorganised sector.

Insurance coverage was a different intervention from strengthening public clinics and hospitals under the rural health mission. Enrolment, access to participating hospitals and protection from out-of-pocket costs need separate assessment. The initial benefit design should not be read as universal health coverage.
India establishes a dedicated tsunami early-warning system

The Indian tsunami early-warning system at INCOIS, Hyderabad, was inaugurated on 15 October 2007. It brought seismic and sea-level observations, modelling and communications into a round-the-clock warning service following the 2004 tsunami.

The system turned lessons from the disaster into an operational public service. Detecting a threat and issuing an advisory are parts of a longer chain: coastal authorities also need to receive warnings, communicate them and organise action.
A farm-debt scheme offers waiver and repayment relief
The Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme launched in May 2008. It offered waiver of eligible debt for small and marginal farmers and conditional relief for other farmers.

Coverage depended on the scheme’s loan and eligibility conditions. It did not cancel every farmer’s debt, including all borrowing outside formal institutions. The CAG later audited implementation, separating the announced design from its delivery.
Climate policy is organised around eight national missions

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh released the National Action Plan on Climate Change on 30 June 2008. It organised priorities around eight national missions addressing climate-related development challenges.

The plan brought adaptation and mitigation into a common policy framework. The missions still required their own design, approval and implementation. The 2008 release therefore helps explain the policy groundwork preceding India’s later Paris commitments and net-zero announcement.
Abhinav Bindra wins India’s first individual Olympic gold
Abhinav Bindra won the men’s 10-metre air rifle event at the Beijing Olympics on 11 August 2008. It was India’s first individual Olympic gold medal.

The individual milestone followed India’s earlier Olympic team successes in hockey. It adds a different sporting achievement to a history often centred on cricket, while leaving questions about training systems and access to facilities open to separate examination.
The global financial crisis reaches India

The international financial crisis affected India through financial markets, capital flows and weaker external demand. From late 2008, the RBI eased monetary conditions and the Union government introduced fiscal support.

India’s exposure differed from economies at the centre of the banking crisis, but it was not insulated from the downturn. Crisis support and the later task of withdrawing it created different policy challenges.
India and the United States signed their civil nuclear cooperation agreement on 10 October 2008, following years of negotiation and an NSG waiver.
It widened the scope for international civilian nuclear cooperation. It did not confer NPT nuclear-weapon State status or resolve every commercial and liability issue.
Chandrayaan-1 launched on 22 October 2008. Findings announced in 2009 included evidence of water and hydroxyl on the lunar surface from NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper aboard the mission.
The discovery combined an Indian mission with international instruments. The launch year and the scientific announcement year should be kept separate.
Coordinated terrorist attacks in Mumbai began on 26 November and continued for several days, striking hotels, a railway station and other locations.

The attacks prompted security changes, including the establishment of the National Investigation Agency and attention to coastal security. These changes require separate evaluation of their implementation.
The NIA Act creates a national investigative institution

The National Investigation Agency Act was enacted on 31 December 2008. It created a framework for a national agency to investigate and prosecute specified offences, with jurisdiction operating alongside state authorities.

The measure followed the Mumbai attacks and formed part of the security response. Its scope concerned offences covered by the statutory framework, rather than every criminal investigation. Agency powers, coordination and safeguards all matter when assessing how the institution worked.
The school expansion effort reaches secondary education
Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan launched in March 2009 to improve access, affordability and quality in secondary education, with a focus on young people aged 15–16.

The programme addressed a stage beyond elementary schooling. It therefore belongs alongside, rather than inside, the right-to-education story. School availability, infrastructure, attendance and learning remained distinct tests of progress.
Elementary education becomes an enforceable right

The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act was enacted in 2009 and came into force on 1 April 2010. It provided a legal framework for free and compulsory elementary education for children aged 6–14.
The law followed the 86th Constitutional Amendment of 2002, which inserted Article 21A. Legal entitlement, school attendance and learning outcomes are different measures of progress.
Aadhaar moves from institution to enrolment
UIDAI was established in 2009. The first Aadhaar number was issued on 29 September 2010.
Aadhaar later became part of welfare and digital service delivery. Identity infrastructure also raised questions about privacy, authentication failures and exclusion. It is not proof of citizenship.
A specialised tribunal for environmental disputes
The National Green Tribunal was established on 18 October 2010 under its 2010 Act to hear specified environmental cases and claims for relief and compensation.

The Tribunal’s establishment followed earlier environmental laws and debates over access to justice. It was not given unlimited jurisdiction over every environmental question. The creation of a forum, the orders it issues and compliance with those orders are distinct measures.
IMPS adds an immediate interbank payment service
NPCI publicly launched Immediate Payment Service on 22 November 2010 after pilot work with banks. The service supported immediate interbank electronic funds transfers.

Instant payments were developing before the later introduction of UPI. IMPS belongs in the sequence between earlier electronic banking systems and the wider retail-payment ecosystem. The infrastructure’s launch and its subsequent reach across banks and customers were separate stages.
The Census records a population above 1.2 billion
The 2011 Census counted India’s population at about 1.21 billion. Its tables provided evidence on the distribution of people, literacy, households and urbanisation.

National totals concealed differences across states, districts and social groups. Census counts, provisional releases and later population projections serve different purposes. Programme coverage should be assessed against the relevant population and eligibility rules.
Civil society campaigns, including Anna Hazare's movement, pressed for stronger anti-corruption institutions and a Lokpal law.
The protests became a major political force. Parliament passed the Lokpal and Lokayuktas legislation in 2013. It received presidential assent in January 2014, with implementation unfolding later.
A livelihoods mission builds around rural self-help groups

The National Rural Livelihoods Mission launched at Banswara, Rajasthan, on 3 June 2011. It restructured the earlier Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana around grassroots institutions, self-help groups, financial links and livelihood support, with an emphasis on women’s participation.

The mission’s approach differed from the employment guarantee: it sought to support livelihoods and collective institutions rather than offer the same statutory guarantee of public work. Group formation and credit access were inputs, not by themselves proof of a lasting increase in household income.
The Supreme Court cancels 122 telecom licences
On 2 February 2012, the Supreme Court quashed 122 telecom licences granted through the challenged 2008 allocation process. The decision scrutinised the fairness of public-resource allocation.

Cancellation of licences through judicial review and proof of criminal wrongdoing are different legal questions. The judgment belongs alongside the history of telecom expansion, regulation and public accountability.
A dedicated law addresses sexual offences against children

The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act came into force on 14 November 2012. It covered persons below 18 and provided for child-friendly reporting, evidence recording, investigation and trial, including designated Special Courts.

The statute preceded the December 2012 Delhi assault and the subsequent criminal-law changes. Its distinct focus was children’s protection throughout the justice process. Designating courts and providing support to children were practical implementation duties, beyond defining offences.
The Delhi assault prompts protests and criminal-law reform

The December 2012 sexual assault in Delhi prompted widespread protests over women’s safety. The Justice J. S. Verma Committee reported in January 2013, followed by an ordinance and the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act.

The Act received assent on 2 April 2013. It changed sexual-offence provisions and addressed offences including stalking, voyeurism and acid attacks. The committee’s recommendations, the enacted law and the quality of policing and justice were separate matters.
The government launched Direct Benefit Transfer on 1 January 2013 to reform delivery processes using information and communication technology. Rollout and scheme coverage expanded over time.

DBT preceded Jan Dhan’s 2014 launch and UPI’s 2016 pilot. They perform different functions: delivery of benefits, access to banking and interoperable payments. Their later combination should not erase their separate origins or the need to assess failed and delayed payments.
Workplace sexual harassment gets a statutory complaints framework

The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 came into force on 9 December 2013. It established duties for employers and mechanisms for complaints and redress.

The law followed the Supreme Court’s earlier Vishaka guidelines. Establishing committees, enabling safe complaints and conducting fair inquiries were practical requirements for making protection accessible. This workplace framework was distinct from the criminal-law amendments.
The taper shock renews pressure on the rupee

Signals in May 2013 of a possible reduction in US monetary stimulus unsettled emerging markets, including India. Capital-flow pressure and rupee volatility prompted measures by the RBI and government.

The episode showed the risks accompanying greater financial integration. The external shock interacted with domestic vulnerabilities. Emergency measures to stabilise markets and longer-term economic changes served different purposes.
Company-law reform adds a corporate responsibility framework

The Companies Act was enacted on 29 August 2013. Section 135 and the associated corporate social responsibility rules took effect on 1 April 2014. They applied to companies meeting specified financial thresholds and set a spending benchmark of at least 2% of average net profits over the preceding three financial years.

The CSR provisions did not apply to every business, and the Act’s provisions commenced in stages. Corporate spending obligations, compliance and the social value of funded activities require different forms of assessment. This was one part of a wider company-law reform.
Food security gains a statutory framework

The National Food Security Act was notified on 10 September 2013 with deemed commencement from 5 July. It established food and nutritional entitlements, including targeted foodgrain coverage for up to 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population.

These are statutory coverage proportions, not poverty rates. Grain production, household access and nutritional outcomes measure different things. The 2013 framework built on an older public distribution system rather than creating food distribution from nothing.
Land acquisition law puts compensation and rehabilitation together
The 2013 land-acquisition law replaced the 1894 framework and came into force on 1 January 2014. It addressed compensation, rehabilitation and resettlement for affected families.

Social-impact assessment and consent requirements depended on the type of acquisition and the Act’s terms. The law did not require identical procedures for every project or settle every conflict over land and livelihoods.
Mangalyaan travels from launch to Mars
The Mars Orbiter Mission launched on 5 November 2013 and entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014.
These milestones span a change of government. The mission is best understood as an institutional achievement across years of scientific work.
A new law links manual-scavenging prohibition with rehabilitation

The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 came into force on 6 December. It addressed insanitary latrines, prohibited employment as manual scavengers and hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks, and provided for identification and rehabilitation.

The law distinguished manual scavenging from hazardous sewer and septic-tank cleaning while addressing both. Enactment did not establish the end of either practice. Identification, safe working methods and rehabilitation remained central to judging its effect.
The southern electricity grid joins the national synchronous network

On 31 December 2013, the southern grid was synchronously connected to the rest of the national power grid through the Raichur–Solapur 765 kV transmission line. The connection facilitated bulk power transfer across regional boundaries.

Grid synchronisation was an engineering milestone after years of regional interconnection. It did not mean that every household had an electricity connection or uninterrupted supply. Generation, transmission capacity and local distribution remained different parts of reliable service.
The Lokpal law follows years of anti-corruption mobilisation
The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 was enacted on 1 January 2014 and came into force on 16 January. It provided a statutory framework for a Union Lokpal and for Lokayuktas in the states.

The law’s title carries 2013, while enactment and commencement fell in 2014. The statute was a milestone in the anti-corruption debate, but passage, appointments and the handling of complaints were separate stages of institution building.
Legislation creates the route to Telangana statehood
The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act received assent on 1 March 2014. Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014, separating from the existing state of Andhra Pradesh.

The legislation followed a long regional movement. Assent and state formation fell on different sides of the change of Union government in May. Division of institutions, resources and administrative responsibilities continued beyond the appointed day.
A public-health campaign reaches a major milestone
India’s last reported case of wild poliovirus occurred in Howrah on 13 January 2011. On 27 March 2014, the WHO South-East Asia Region, including India, was certified polio-free.

The result followed sustained vaccination, surveillance and work by public-health staff and partner organisations across many years. Regional certification was not a declaration of worldwide eradication, and it did not remove the need to vaccinate and monitor for poliovirus.
overview: The 2004 change of government was followed by several forms of public action. RTI opened access to official records, the employment guarantee created a statutory claim to public work, and the rural health mission sought stronger services. Urban renewal focused on cities, while health insurance addressed hospital costs for eligible poor households. Women’s protections and forest rights dealt with other forms of exclusion.

The period also built institutions and infrastructure. A tsunami-warning system followed the coastal disaster; climate policy was organised around national missions. The financial crisis prompted monetary easing and fiscal support, while farm debt relief addressed agricultural credit. Mumbai’s attacks were followed by the NIA framework. Aadhaar, IMPS, school programmes and rural livelihoods took different approaches to access and opportunity.

The closing years brought anti-corruption protests, the spectrum judgment and demands for women’s safety after the Delhi assault. Food security, land acquisition, sanitation work and company law received new statutory frameworks. The Lokpal law commenced in January 2014. Southern-grid synchronisation marked an infrastructure milestone, while Telangana’s formation and the Mars mission crossed into the next era. Abhinav Bindra’s Olympic gold adds a sporting achievement to this wider account.

eras.title: Digital Transformation & Modern Geopolitics
eras.question: What does transformation look like in daily life?
eras.intro: The 2014 election brought a single-party majority within the NDA government. Banking access, sanitation, digital services and tax reform became major priorities. Constitutional disputes, border crises and the pandemic tested institutions. Space missions and diplomacy brought prominent milestones, while the 2024 result increased the importance of coalition partners.
eras.tension: These years remain unfinished history. A launch, a law, an election result and a measured public outcome describe different things. The chapter tracks selected milestones through April 2026, with dates and source records kept separate from claims about lasting success.
events: The BJP wins a majority and Modi takes office
The BJP won 282 Lok Sabha seats in the 2014 election. Narendra Modi took office as prime minister on 26 May, heading an NDA government.

A single party held a Lok Sabha majority for the first time since the 1984 election. Allies remained part of the government. The result changed the parliamentary balance after decades dominated by coalition and minority governments.
Jan Dhan makes financial inclusion a national mission
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana launched on 28 August 2014 with a drive to extend banking access to unbanked households.

The programme followed earlier banking and inclusion initiatives. Opening an account is a measurable step, but regular use, access to withdrawals and successful receipt of benefits are different outcomes. The number of accounts should not automatically be treated as the number of newly banked people.
Make in India launched on 25 September 2014 to encourage investment and manufacturing.
It belongs at the start of this period, rather than being described as a new 2024 initiative. Programme goals and measured manufacturing outcomes are different claims.
Swachh Bharat Mission launched on 2 October 2014, with rural and urban components addressing sanitation and cleanliness.

Toilet construction, sustained use, water availability and safe waste management are different parts of sanitation. Programme declarations and administrative coverage figures require separate scrutiny of conditions experienced by households and workers.
NITI Aayog replaces the Planning Commission

A government resolution dated 1 January 2015 replaced the Planning Commission with NITI Aayog, the National Institution for Transforming India. The new institution’s remit included policy strategy and advice to the Union and states.

The change revisited an institution founded in 1950. Replacing the commission changed the machinery of national policy coordination; it did not mean that public investment or development planning ended. Its role needs examination alongside the separate institutions governing budgets and finance.
Digital India brings services and connectivity into one programme
Digital India launched on 1 July 2015 to advance digital infrastructure, public services and digital empowerment.

The programme built on earlier computerisation, telecom networks and online services. Providing a digital service also required connectivity, accessible design, reliable authentication and ways to resolve failures. Digitising a process did not guarantee access for everyone.
Real-estate regulation adds protections for homebuyers

The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act was enacted on 25 March 2016. Its framework provided for project registration, disclosures, regulatory authorities and adjudication, with provisions brought into force in stages.

The law’s coverage and exemptions mattered to individual projects. Enactment, state-level rules, functioning authorities and remedies for delayed projects were separate steps. Regulation did not eliminate every risk faced by a buyer.
UPI connects bank accounts in real time
NPCI's Unified Payments Interface had its pilot launch on 11 April 2016, before demonetisation. It enabled instant payments across participating banks.
UPI built on an existing banking and payments system. Its later adoption should not be reduced to a single policy or a single political term.
An electronic platform links agricultural markets

The National Agriculture Market, e-NAM, launched on 14 April 2016 in 21 mandis across eight states, initially with pilot trading in 24 commodities. It sought to connect existing regulated markets through a common electronic trading platform.

Digitising market transactions was distinct from the later farm laws and their repeal. Platform access, quality assessment, settlement and physical movement of produce remained separate requirements. Registration alone does not establish better prices for every farmer.
Ujjwala supports access to LPG cooking connections

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana launched at Ballia, Uttar Pradesh, on 1 May 2016. It provided deposit-free LPG connections in the names of adult women from eligible poor households, seeking to widen access to cleaner cooking fuel.

Obtaining a connection and using LPG regularly are different measures. Refill affordability, local supply and continued use of other fuels matter when assessing household benefits. The programme’s launch should therefore be distinguished from later expansion and sustained fuel use.
A new framework for insolvency resolution

The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was enacted on 28 May 2016. It created a consolidated legal framework for insolvency resolution and related processes, with provisions brought into force through notifications.

Enactment did not make every part of the framework operational on the same day. Assessing its results requires distinguishing resolutions from liquidations and examining recovery, delay and the value of the assets involved. This entry describes the 2016 milestone, rather than every later amendment.
Interest-rate decisions move to a statutory committee

A six-member Monetary Policy Committee was constituted on 29 September 2016 under the amended RBI Act. It comprised three internal and three external members and was tasked with determining the policy rate to achieve the inflation target.

The reform changed how monetary-policy decisions were made and accounted for. A committee decision and the subsequent path of inflation are different things: food supply, fuel prices and other economic conditions also affect prices. The institutional change belongs alongside the era’s financial reforms.
India signed the Paris Agreement on 22 April 2016 and ratified it on 2 October 2016, according to the UNFCCC treaty record.

Ratification placed India within the agreement’s international framework. It was distinct from the later 2070 net-zero announcement and from domestic implementation of climate policy. Treaty participation, national commitments and measured emissions outcomes are different milestones.
On 8 November, the government announced withdrawal of the legal-tender status of existing ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes, subject to specified exceptions and exchange arrangements.
The policy caused a major cash disruption. Claims about lasting effects on black money, counterfeiting, formalisation or digital adoption require evidence beyond the announcement itself.
Disability law broadens its rights framework

The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 replaced the earlier 1995 legislation and expanded the recognised disability categories from seven to twenty-one. It addressed rights and duties across areas including education, employment and accessibility.

The legislation represented a broader framework, rather than proof that physical, digital and social barriers had disappeared. Some provisions distinguish persons with disabilities from persons with benchmark disabilities. The categories should not be treated as interchangeable.
Goods and Services Tax rolled out on 1 July 2017 following a constitutional amendment and negotiation between the Union and states.
GST subsumed many indirect taxes through a dual Union–state framework. It did not replace every indirect tax or create a single tax rate for all goods and services.
Privacy is recognised as a fundamental right
On 24 August 2017, a nine-judge Supreme Court bench recognised the constitutional protection of privacy in the Puttaswamy case.

The decision gave constitutional weight to questions about personal information, dignity and state power. It should be distinguished from the separate Aadhaar judgment in 2018 and from later legislation on data protection.
The Supreme Court reads down Section 377
On 6 September 2018, the Supreme Court in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India held Section 377 unconstitutional insofar as it criminalised consensual sexual conduct between adults of the same sex.

The decision addressed criminalisation and constitutional protections of dignity, liberty and equality. It should not be described as a judgment that established same-sex marriage. Legal reform and the lived experience of discrimination remain distinct subjects.
PM-JAY adds publicly financed hospital cover
Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana launched on 23 September 2018 in Ranchi. Its design provided health cover for eligible families for specified secondary and tertiary hospital care.

Hospital treatment cover is not the same as universal access to every kind of health care. Primary care, outpatient costs, provider availability and treatment quality require separate attention. This entry describes the launch; later eligibility expansions are separate milestones.
A national programme coordinates action on air pollution
The National Clean Air Programme launched on 10 January 2019 as a national strategy to tackle air pollution through coordinated action, including city-level plans.

The programme built on the earlier legal framework of pollution-control boards. Plans and spending need to be assessed against monitored pollution, local sources and implementation. A launch or a target is not a measured improvement in the air people breathe.
Pulwama is followed by the Balakot air strike

The Pulwama terrorist attack killed 40 CRPF personnel on 14 February 2019. India carried out an air strike at Balakot in Pakistan on 26 February, describing its target as a Jaish-e-Mohammed training camp.

The attack and military response intensified India–Pakistan tensions. Official statements establish the positions taken by the governments. Claims about strike casualties and the wider military outcome require independent evidence beyond those statements.
Chandrayaan-2 reaches lunar orbit but misses its soft landing

Chandrayaan-2 launched on 22 July 2019 with an orbiter, lander and rover. The September soft-landing attempt was unsuccessful, while the orbiter continued scientific observations with its instruments.

The mission had different outcomes for its components. Orbital science continued despite the loss of the landing objective. This sequence helps explain the later Chandrayaan-3 landing without treating exploration as an uninterrupted series of successes.
August constitutional measures rendered Article 370's special-status provisions inoperative. Reorganisation took effect on 31 October, creating the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.
The August constitutional change and October administrative reorganisation were distinct steps. Their effects on rights, representation and security require attention beyond the legal announcements.
Ration portability begins across two interstate clusters

Interstate ration-card portability was inaugurated on 9 August 2019 between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and between Gujarat and Maharashtra. The pilot formed an early stage of One Nation One Ration Card, using electronic point-of-sale systems and authentication to deliver existing food entitlements away from a beneficiary’s home location.

Portability changed where eligible people accessed their ration, rather than creating a new food entitlement. The four-state pilot was not nationwide coverage. Authentication, shop access and awareness remained practical issues, particularly for migrant households.
Rural tap-water provision becomes a national mission

Jal Jeevan Mission was announced on 15 August 2019 and implemented with states and Union Territories. Its design sought household tap-water service in rural areas, with adequate quantity, prescribed quality and regular long-term supply.

A tap connection is one part of a functioning water service. Source sustainability, water quality, maintenance and regular delivery are separate tests. The mission’s original target dates should not be treated as evidence that every household received the intended service.
Citizenship rules change for specified migrant groups

The Citizenship (Amendment) Act received assent on 12 December 2019. It created a citizenship route for eligible Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered India on or before 31 December 2014, subject to its conditions.

The religion-based eligibility generated disputes over equality and citizenship policy. The amendment did not itself remove the citizenship of existing Indian citizens. Implementation rules were notified on 11 March 2024, a separate step from enactment.
A dedicated transgender-rights law comes into force

The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 came into force on 10 January 2020 under its Gazette commencement notification. The original framework addressed recognition of identity, non-discrimination in education and employment, healthcare and welfare measures.

This entry records the law’s commencement and original scope. Legal recognition, administrative procedures and people’s experience of access and discrimination require separate examination. A statutory protection does not by itself establish equal treatment in everyday life.
COVID-19 brought lockdowns, migration distress and severe pressure on health services. India began its national vaccination programme on 16 January 2021.

Covaxin was developed in India. Covishield was manufactured in India from the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine. Vaccine Maitri involved overseas supplies and was distinct from the domestic vaccination campaign.
PLI programmes expanded across 14 manufacturing sectors, with a ₹1.97 lakh crore outlay announced in the 2021–22 Union Budget.

Incentive commitments are not the same as realised investment, employment or domestic value addition. Those outcomes need sector-specific assessment. Energy transition also remains an ongoing policy area.
The Galwan clash deepens the border crisis with China
Indian and Chinese troops clashed in the Galwan Valley on 15 June 2020 during the eastern Ladakh border standoff. Twenty Indian military personnel died.

The clash damaged trust and placed the border dispute at the centre of bilateral relations. A particular disengagement agreement and a final settlement of the boundary are different outcomes. Claims about who controlled specific locations require dated evidence.
NEP 2020 sets out a new education framework

The Union Cabinet approved National Education Policy 2020 on 29 July. It proposed changes across school and higher education, including a 5+3+3+4 curricular and pedagogical structure that included early childhood education.

The proposal followed earlier national policies and a multi-year consultation process. Cabinet approval did not mean that every institution changed immediately. Implementation depended on subsequent decisions and action across governments and educational bodies.

Parliament passed three farm laws in September 2020. Following sustained farmer protests, Parliament passed repeal legislation in November 2021. The Farm Laws Repeal Act received assent on 30 November.

The repeal reversed those legislative changes. It did not, by itself, resolve wider disputes over agricultural markets, procurement or minimum support prices. Policy design and the process of building public consent are both part of this history.
Neeraj Chopra wins Olympic javelin gold
Neeraj Chopra won the men’s javelin final at the Tokyo Olympics on 7 August 2021 with a best throw of 87.58 metres. He became the first Indian to win an Olympic gold medal in athletics.

The result followed Abhinav Bindra’s individual Olympic gold in shooting in 2008 and India’s earlier team successes. It gives athletics its own place in the sporting timeline rather than folding every achievement into cricket’s history.
Gati Shakti seeks coordinated infrastructure planning
PM Gati Shakti, a national master plan for multimodal connectivity, launched on 13 October 2021. It sought to improve coordination of infrastructure planning across ministries and networks.

Roads, railways, ports and other connections serve the same journeys and supply chains. Coordinating plans addresses their interfaces, while construction, service quality and logistics costs remain tests of delivery. The launch of a planning framework was not completion of its proposed infrastructure.
At COP26 on 1 November 2021, India announced a target of net-zero emissions by 2070 alongside commitments concerning non-fossil capacity and other measures for 2030.

A target is a commitment about the future. Installed electricity capacity, electricity generated, total energy use and economy-wide emissions measure different things. Progress in one does not establish that every climate objective has been achieved.
Agnipath introduces a new route into military service

The government approved the Agnipath recruitment scheme on 14 June 2022. Its original design provided four years of service for recruits known as Agniveers, with provision to select up to 25% of each specific batch for the regular cadre under the scheme’s criteria.

The announcement changed the recruitment and service model for the covered intake. The four-year engagement, selection for longer service and employment after exit were different stages. Retention ceilings should not be read as a guarantee that every batch would retain the maximum share.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission set out a framework for developing production, demand and infrastructure for green hydrogen.
It is one part of a wider energy transition. Announced targets describe intended outcomes, rather than hydrogen already produced or emissions already avoided.
A research mission backs quantum technologies

The Union Cabinet approved the National Quantum Mission on 19 April 2023, with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023–24 to 2030–31. Its research programme covered quantum computing, communication, sensing and materials or devices.

The approval funded a research agenda with future deliverables. It was not a claim that the planned computing or communication capabilities had already been achieved. Funding, research institutions, working demonstrations and deployable systems mark different stages.
Digital personal data gets a dedicated statutory framework

The Digital Personal Data Protection Act received assent on 11 August 2023. It set out a framework for processing digital personal data, with obligations for those handling it and rights and duties for individuals.

Enactment did not bring every provision into force immediately. Rules notified in November 2025 used phased commencement, including later dates for several requirements. The 2017 constitutional privacy judgment and this statutory framework address related but distinct questions.
A soft landing in the Moon's southern high latitudes
Chandrayaan-3 successfully soft-landed on 23 August 2023. India became the fourth country to achieve a lunar soft landing.
The landing site was around 69° south latitude. It was in the southern high-latitude region, not at the geographic south pole itself.
The New Delhi summit on 9–10 September adopted a leaders' declaration. The African Union joined the G20 as a permanent member.
The declaration recorded negotiated commitments on development and international cooperation. Summit agreements and their later implementation should be assessed separately.
A constitutional amendment provides for women’s legislative reservation
The 106th Constitutional Amendment received assent on 28 September 2023. It provided for one-third reservation for women in Lok Sabha, state legislative assemblies and the Delhi assembly.

The reservation was tied to a delimitation exercise after publication of relevant figures from the first census taken after commencement. The amendment did not immediately reserve one-third of seats in the 2024 election. Local-government reservations had a separate, earlier constitutional history.
The Ram temple consecration takes place in Ayodhya
The consecration ceremony at the Ram temple in Ayodhya took place on 22 January 2024, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi participating.

The ceremony followed the Supreme Court’s November 2019 decision on the land dispute. The 1992 demolition, the court’s judgment and the temple ceremony were distinct events within a longer political, religious and legal history.
The Supreme Court strikes down electoral bonds
On 15 February 2024, the Supreme Court held the Electoral Bond Scheme unconstitutional. The decision addressed political-funding transparency and voters’ access to information.

The judgment and the subsequent disclosure of donation records were separate steps. A donor–recipient entry establishes a recorded financial connection. It does not, without further evidence, prove a corrupt exchange or explain a particular government decision.
The BJP won 240 Lok Sabha seats and Congress 99. The BJP fell short of a majority on its own, and an NDA coalition returned to government under Narendra Modi.
The result differed from the BJP's single-party majorities in 2014 and 2019. It renewed the importance of allies within the governing coalition.
Three new laws begin a transition in criminal justice

Most provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam came into force on 1 July 2024. They replaced the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act frameworks, subject to transitional provisions.

The changes concerned offences, procedure and evidence. Earlier events and pending proceedings required attention to the applicable law and savings provisions. New statutory text also required training, systems and consistent practice across police, courts and forensic services.
Assembly elections return in Jammu and Kashmir
Jammu and Kashmir held assembly polling in three phases from 18 September to 1 October 2024. Omar Abdullah took oath as chief minister on 16 October.

These were the first assembly elections after the 2019 reorganisation. Restoring an elected assembly and restoring statehood were separate questions. The election took place under the Union Territory framework.
ISRO successfully docked the two SpaDeX satellites on 16 January 2025.
The experiment demonstrated a capability relevant to future missions requiring spacecraft to meet and connect in orbit. It did not itself constitute an operational Indian space station.
Pahalgam is followed by Operation Sindoor and cross-border fighting

The terrorist attack at Pahalgam on 22 April 2025 killed 26 people. India launched Operation Sindoor on 7 May, stating that it targeted terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Military exchanges followed.

On 10 May, both sides agreed to halt firing and military action. The attack, strikes and agreement were separate stages. Official briefings record each side’s account; claims about battle damage, casualties and responsibility need evidence beyond a single government’s narrative.
NISAR adds a joint Earth-observation mission
The joint NASA–ISRO NISAR mission launched on 30 July 2025 aboard GSLV-F16.
The mission extends the space story beyond lunar exploration to observing the Earth. Its joint development also illustrates the continuing role of international scientific cooperation.
WHO records fifteen years without a regional wild-polio case
On 13 January 2026, WHO reported that its South-East Asia Region had sustained its polio-free status fifteen years after the last wild-poliovirus case, recorded in India in 2011.

This is a dated regional status report that includes India, rather than a claim of global eradication. WHO emphasised continued vaccination and surveillance against importation. Sustaining an achievement is a separate public-health task from reaching certification.
India and the EU conclude free-trade negotiations
India and the European Union announced the conclusion of free-trade agreement negotiations on 27 January 2026. Talks had first opened in 2007, paused in 2013 and resumed in 2022.

Concluding negotiations was a diplomatic and commercial milestone. Legal revision, signature, approval and entry into force were further stages. The announcement did not itself activate every proposed tariff reduction or establish the agreement’s eventual effect on jobs and trade.
New Delhi hosts the AI Impact Summit
India hosted the AI Impact Summit in February 2026. The New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact set out shared aims for international cooperation, wider access to AI resources and trusted systems.

The summit’s declaration and collaborative initiatives were voluntary frameworks. Announced investment, available computing capacity and services people could actually use were separate measures. The event extended the digital-policy story into international AI governance.
A new GDP series changes the statistical benchmark

On 27 February 2026, MoSPI released a new series of annual and quarterly national accounts with 2022–2023 as its base year, replacing the 2011–2012 series. The revision incorporated updated data and methods.

A revised estimate changes how economic activity is measured. It is not additional production created on release day. Comparisons across decades need consistent series, price bases and revision dates, particularly when assessing claims about growth under different governments.
Census 2027 begins its housing and houselisting phase

Phase I of Census 2027 began on 1 April 2026 with digital self-enumeration in the first set of participating areas. Enumerator visits in those areas were scheduled from 16 April, within a phased national window extending from April to September.

This phase collected information about housing, amenities and household assets. It was distinct from the later population-enumeration phase. The start of houselisting did not provide a new completed national population total to replace the 2011 Census.
The new income-tax statute comes into force
The Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026. It replaced the 1961 statute for the new framework and used the term tax year for income earned from the 2026–2027 financial year onwards.

Earlier tax years and related proceedings remained subject to transitional provisions. A new statute, an annual change in tax rates and the rules governing a particular year’s return were different matters. The transition required the administration to handle both legal frameworks.
A constitutional proposal fails to secure the required majority

After discussion on 16 and 17 April 2026, the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill did not secure the special majority required for its motion for consideration. The dependent delimitation and Union Territories bills were not taken further in that session.

The proposals concerned legislative representation for women and delimitation. The bill remained a proposal rather than becoming a constitutional amendment. Its outcome belongs alongside the separate 106th Amendment enacted in 2023 and the conditions attached to that earlier framework.
